Kryptonite New York 1210 Bike Chain Lock, 3.25 Feet Long Heavy Duty Anti-Theft Sold Secure Gold Bicycle Chain Lock with Evolution Disc Lock and Keys for Ultimate Security E-Bike, Motorcycle, Scooter I own a chain just like this. See my review here: [[ASIN:B000AMVPUM Kryptonite New York Chain 3' With Key Lock]]

The problem with these giant chains is a sense of added security, but I'm not convinced you get it with something like this. Big bolt cutters will demolish this thing (for evidence, search youtube for "security chains vs. bolt choppers", skip to 6min24s... this chain gets demolished in less than a minute. Granted, they're huge bolt cutters. But someone running around in a van at 3AM isn't going to care.). Couple the questionable security with how big of a pain this thing is to lug around (I've owned the chain for years) and I can't imagine it's worth it.

Anyway, since no bike lock seems to be impervious to bike theft, it's important for people to realize the only true security is to store the bike within sight (your home, place of work, near you on a restaurant patio, etc.). I imagine the latest and greatest u-locks are a better option due to the shear time it takes to grind through them (with bolt cutters not being an option), but I'd wager all bike chains are susceptible to big bolt cutters.
text_fidelity_b: Kryptonite New York 1210 Bike Chain Lock, 3.25 Feet Long Heavy Duty Anti-Theft Sold Secure Gold Bicycle Chain Lock with Evolution Disc Lock and Keys for Ultimate Security E-Bike, Motorcycle, Scooter

text_fidelity_a:
Freeze Dried Sliced Strawberries by Nutristore | Pack of 2 | Healthy Snack | Emergency Survival Bulk Food Storage | Amazing Taste & Quality | 25 Year Shelf Life These strawberries are beyond delicious! These big #10 (one gallon) cans of freeze dried fruit are IDEAL if you are new to using freeze dried fruits or if you want to put away a couple cans for your family in case of emergency but you don't want to spend $150 on a 6 can case plus shipping from somewhere else. (You simply cannot beat Amazon Prime!)

• • • #10 cans typically hold 12 cups of food and about 11 cups of freeze dried fruits and veggies • • •

It is hard to find information about how much food is actually in a #10 can and have it be accurate enough that you can plan your meals. When filled to the brim with something like rice, the #10 cans hold 12 cups. But freeze dried food is light and not compacted, with air space between the dry pieces so you get about 11 cups (bananas) to 11.25 cups (strawberries and raspberries) in a big can like this. The cans are "full", the difference is simply air space between the fruit pieces. (To be safe, always assume there are 11 cups per #10 can of freeze dried fruits and veggies. I have found this to be accurate and a great way to calculate how much you have stored.)

Now let's talk about how yummy the food is! As I took pictures I could hardly stop my 9 year old son from grabbing handfuls of strawberries behind my back as I tried to snap a quick photo. (The bowl of strawberries was dumped straight into his mouth mere seconds after I got that picture!) The fruit is positively DELICIOUS for snacking straight from the can!

We live in Houston and personally lived through Hurricane Ike in 2008. At the time my son was 18 months old and I would have given anything - ANYTHING - to have these freeze dried strawberries to have offered him. Grocery stores were picked clean the day before the storm. Some of the grocery stores flooded and most of them had damage to roofs, glass doors and building structures from being hit by flung tree branches, fence pieces and debris. We went 12 days without electricity in our home. Grocery stores were without power for the first 5 or 6 days and stayed closed for about a week in our area as they had to be cleaned up before reopening. It was almost 3 weeks after the storm before stores were restocked with fresh produce beyond a few local items like tomatoes and jalapeños. Please, take the advice from someone who has lived through a natural disaster and invest in freeze dried fruits and veggies for your family. Everything in our refrigerators and freezers were ruined by day 2 without power and we still had 10 days to go. The only thing you have to rely on is what you have on your pantry shelves. That is it. These cans will keep for 25 years unopened and truly are a wise investment.

So, since I have been through a natural disaster, I have learned how to bake with freeze dried food since I still live in Houston and may have to deal with another storm in the future. These strawberries did GREAT and I'm going to include the recipe I used so you can have success with them, too. It is wise to open and try the food you are storing but since this company gave several reviewers like myself a discount to test their products, this work has been done for you. You can simply store the cans of food knowing it is superior quality. (I have purchased and used Thrive brand fruits and these taste identical to theirs! In my opinion these strawberries were even better quality.)

• Strawberry Chocolate Chip Muffins •
--> This recipe also works with freeze dried blueberries or other freeze dried fruits
1/4 cup butter, softened
1/3 cup sugar
1 egg, beaten
1/2 cup milk (a small can of evaporated milk is fine to use)
1 cup flour (up to 1.5 cups depending on humidity; batter should be a thick muffin batter)
1 and 1/2 tsp baking powder
1/2 cup freeze dried strawberries (or raspberries or other fruit) rehydrated in 1/2 cup water with the excess liquid drained off
1/2 cup milk chocolate chips

Preheat oven to 400°. Cream butter and sugar. Add the egg and mix well. Add flour alternately with splashes of milk and combine until a thick batter has formed and all ingredients are incorporated. Gently fold in rehydrated fruit. Spoon into 12 paper lined baking cups, filling halfway to 3/4ths full. Bake for 20 minutes or until tops begin to turn golden.

• Tip •
The leftover powder at the bottom of each can is AWESOME for making strawberry butter or adding to oatmeal to make your own fruit and cream flavor. If nothing else, dump the powder in your pancake batter. Don't let the powder go to waste, it is delicious!

Also, if you want to know about the countries of origin on the fruits, this was posted on the seller's FAQ page: "We source our Nutristore foods from some of the following countries: USA, Canada, Ecuador, Greece, Costa Rica, Uruguay, Argentina, Serbia, New Zealand, India, Poland, Mexico & Chile. [We] no longer source foods from China."

I was very fortunate to be able to purchase this pack of freeze dried strawberries at a discount so I could try it, eat it and bake with it before writing a review. I hope that by sharing my photos and experience that you are able to make the best buying decision for your own family! Hugs from Houston!
text_fidelity_b: Freeze Dried Sliced Strawberries by Nutristore | Pack of 2 | Healthy Snack | Emergency Survival Bulk Food Storage | Amazing Taste & Quality | 25 Year Shelf Life

text_fidelity_a:
Black Diamond Spot Headlamp My favorite low priced headlamp.
Not the quality of high tech wonder lamps. But there are no real faults. And the interface is very good.
All inputs on one button which is the best way to do it, fewer moving parts to go wrong.
3 inputs : momentary push, 3 second push, 6 second push.
If the lamp is on :
Momentary push cycles on/off.
Long push gradually dims the light in steps.
(when it reaches the dimmest it will flicker once to indicate lowest level,
then it gradually brightens the light, step at a time, flickers once on highest).
This works very well to set the brightness levels.

When light is OFF:
momentary push turns it on (two outer lights for flood, or center for spot. Repeat pushes will alternate: spot, off, flood, off, spot,...
3 second push : turns on the red lamp
6 second push: turns on the lock mode (locks lamp off until another 6 sec. push turns it back on. A blue light on the side will go on for a couple seconds to verify the lamp is locked).

I find the interface easy to use to get it to do as I like when I like.
5 different tilt settings from straight down to higher than straight forward. There are settings I find perfect for reading or watching your step on the trail. And they stay put.

Very bright on spot!
The flood is very spread out, lights up the whole room or tent.

5 stars.
------

Another lamp that costs about $10 more is the Princeton Tec EOS TACTICAL. The tactical model of the EOS line is military issue from several governments. Bulletproof and rugged, really waterproof. But the ergonomics are military rough: the button is very hard to push (so it won't wear out), the battery box takes a tool like a dime to open (so they could never fall out by mistake). A better choice if you going to climb mount Everest and your life depends on the lamp. Not as good as this BDSH for using in common outdoor camping, running, hunting, imo.

Those are the two under $50 that I like.

EDIT: I should have noted the reviews stating the tilt lock stops would fail. They failed in 6 months on one of mine of these. The other two I have are getting weaker and weaker (about a year old). Then the lamp just tilts all the way forward and points at your toes. No way to reset the tilt after the mechanism breaks. I changed my rating from 5 stars to 2 stars. I do NOT recommend these.
text_fidelity_b: Black Diamond Spot Headlamp

EZX by EZ Lab EZX-SU361775GY Slim Under The Desk Electric Folding Quiet Anti-Shock Treadmill Hydraulic Armrest Home Office Exercise Body Induction Smart, Gray, 55" x 28.5" x 52" I was hesitant about purchasing this but, I decided to take a risk after seeing comparables online that were more expensive. The treadmill stores easily on the wall and I can move it into place whenever I want to use it. It is easy to control the roll even on a hardwood floor.

For Setup:
1. Place a little lube between the platform and running belt (Oil is included)

For Use:
1. Best to use on a hard surface (Hardwood / Tile)
2. Plug in Treadmill (Fold Handle Up if Needed - Highly suggested for initial use)
3. Stand on the end opposite of the digital readouts
4. Slowly take THREE steps forward (3 dashes stacked up on top of each other will appear on the digital readout)
5. The treadmill will slowly begin to move and continue to increase speed while you walk close to the readout screen
6. To hold a certain speed, walk on the middle section of the treadmill
7. To slow down, walk on the end furthest away from the digital readout
8. Keep in mind the machine will continue to speed up when you walk closest to the digital readout AND it will continue to slow down when you walk furthest from the readout, until it comes to a stop
9. If it comes to a stop and you want to continue your session, step off the treadmill and go back to step 3 of this section

It does take practice to get familiar with the treadmill and how speed adjustments are made. During familiarization, I suggest using the support handle that is on the machine. This is not your typical treadmill that has speed adjustment buttons. Hence, it will take time getting used to how it operates so be careful in the beginning.

For Belt Adjustment:
1. A wrench is included in the box
2. If the running belt tends to slide to the right during use, loosen the adjustment screw on the right side (the screw is on the opposite end of the digital readout)
3. If the running belt tends to slide to the left during use, loosen the adjustment screw on the left
4. Make 1/2 to 1/4 turn adjustments (extreme adjustments can make the tuning process more frustrating)
5. Take your time

I've always unplugged the machine after each use and store it against a wall. The running belt "ran" away from me a couple of times when I first got the treadmill and I prevented my fall by using the handrail. Every time I've had an issue with the speed on the treadmill, it's been due to operator error. I've had to remind myself and be cognizant of the fact that speed adjustments are done differently on this treadmill. I wanted something new, intuitive, easy to store, easy to move, and easy to operate. This treadmill met my criteria and is well designed and built.

I watched a lot of videos online before I purchased it. By the time it arrived, I was familiar with how to use it, what to avoid, and possible safety issues I'd have to keep in mind. I recommend this treadmill for OFFICE USE, WALKING, and LIGHT JOGS. For a workout, I recommend using a traditional treadmill with manual speed & incline adjustments.
text_fidelity_b: EZX by EZ Lab EZX-SU361775GY Slim Under The Desk Electric Folding Quiet Anti-Shock Treadmill Hydraulic Armrest Home Office Exercise Body Induction Smart, Gray, 55" x 28.5" x 52"

Topeak Mondo Pack with Fixer F25 with Extendable Back Pocket, 12.6 x 5.1 x 6.3-Inch (X-Large) A great product, certainly up to Topeak's standards. The pouch is huge and very roomy. It has a great side compartment to prevent your tools from beating up your snacks, and has a nice mesh pocket perfect for CO2 cartridges. Two caveats are worth considering. First, there is a temptation to stuff the main compartment full of stuff, and this is a great idea for a long ride. If you do so, it will require some unpacking to get to all of the gear, so pack the stuff you want to access quickly (e.g. food!) near the zipper. You can pack the tubes out of the way, if you blow one, you likely don't have a problem with the extra minute it takes you to get to it. The second issue to be aware of is that this pack is HUGE. Measure your bike to make sure that it fits, and make sure that you are happy with the look (it looks nothing like a wedge pack).

I was aware of both issues, and I love the pack! It lets me ride VERY long rides on my road bike without support and without a trunk bag.

Belly and side reflective is large and bright. Two smaller shoulder stripes in the back and four in the front round out the reflective coverage. The velcro (sorry, hook and loop) fasteners on the side are such that should have no trouble fastened. Then comes the LED lighting. It’s crazy bright! Green in color with three on settings: Steady on, fast blink, slow blink and off. The battery back rests in a special velcro-closed pocket in the back of the center front of the vest. There is a push button micro switch in the front of the vest to turn on the light. There is also a master on-off switch on the small battery-switch unit, and the USB micro-b charging port is there as well. There are visible wires coming out of the battery pack, connected to the LED ends, but the pocket seems to be substantial and protective enough that, barring abuse, should hold up pretty well. This is not a lightweight vest, but if you’re getting out in the dark, go safely. This is a great vest to do it.

There were some very good points that I needn't repeat in this review. I encourage anyone purchasing this dart board to read all the reviews to glean assembly hints.

The dart board came in one box and the box was a little beat up. None of the components were damaged though. Despite the outside condition of the box it was packaged well inside.

I read all the instructions before assembling. I utilized a small handle screw driver for assembly so I would be less likely to over tighten them and damage the press board. I did deviate from the instructions slightly. After assembling the main cabinet (the lower or base cabinet) I put the back on it while it was laying flat on the floor (be sure to line up the bottom of the back with the bottom of the bottom shelf, not the sides). This allowed me ensure that the cabinet was square before installing the door or the top. I installed the top section after standing up the cabinet.

Following the steps above should eliminate any door sag, or at least it did in my case. The completed unit is quite sound stable enough. However I did anchor it to the wall with a couple of L brackets at the top of the completed unit. I did not find it necessary to add any other brackets as others have indicated. We play on the board virtually every day and have had zero problems.

Why not 5 stars? The board has a function that allows you to play against the computer. It does not work on our board. Every thing else works, and it looks great. Best dart board I have ever had. I will be adding some lights in the canopy.

text_fidelity_a:
Mirrycle MTB Bar End Mountain Bicycle Mirror , Black Just installed the Mirrycle bicycle mirror today and took it for a test run.

A few observations and comments.

Agreed, assembly is not entirely easy. As mentioned by numerous reviews, the screws drive hard to the point that you think you’re actually cracking the plastic plus the included Allen wrench requires some strength to turn. But not to worry. Read the instructions and they’ll confirm the hard drive and that you will not crack the plastic. I didn’t try WD40 or any other lubricant so cannot say if that would ease the assembly.

I installed the Mirrycle onto a GT hybrid bicycle and after using a Dremel tool to create an opening in the end of my handle grip I found the handlebar opening accepted the smaller of the two wedges for mounting. I chose to follow the alternative down and under installation mentioned on Amazon reviews which is quite clever and works very well however I believe you may get a better site picture using the “normal” above and to the side installation which would facilitate not having to move your eyes so far from your frontal path to do so. The primary disadvantage to the “normal” up-and-out installation is that the mirror really sticks out there very exposed and if/when you dump your bike or ride close to any shrubs, etc., your mirror will be the early casualty, plus the storage shed where we keep our bikes is small which would necessitate tucking the mirror in upon each return. Do whichever works best for you.

From the lower mounting position I could see both myself and directly behind me but I don’t believe that provides the maximum field of view. On my initial trip I stopped a couple times to adjust the mirror in a similar manner to what you would do with a car, i.e., if you can see part of yourself/your bike in the mirror, tilt it out just a little further until you can’t and that should be about right. Once adjusted properly you only need to tilt your head a tad one way to see either part of yourself directly behind the mirror or a tad the other way to see much more of the road to your direct left.

I was amazed at how solid this mirror rode exhibiting absolutely no jitter or vibration. The large convex shape offered a wide, clear field of view which allowed me not only to see what was coming from behind me but also what was to the near left rear of me as well.

This was only my first day with this product but I’m impressed with the quality and the flexible mounting options it offers.
text_fidelity_b: Mirrycle MTB Bar End Mountain Bicycle Mirror , Black

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in)) ***Update after 16 months of gentle use***

Fell apart after 16 months of gentle use; largely in an office environment. Was a five star item, but honestly I expect at least 24 months of life in this scenario. Until then the band worked well, but the heart rate feature was hit and miss.

**Original Review**
I got this for the misses to help her keep track of her activities and keep things somewhat interesting (she likes the Fitbit app). She previously had the Fitbit Zip, and I wanted to find something that was harder to forget in a pair of pants (and thus get washed).

Getting this set up was a breeze, though like her Zip, this was easier to get working on her Android phone than Mac Pro. A nice (though not unexpected) plus was the ability to simply replace one device with another and keep her progress. Here are some general observations:
Pros:
The stair tracker is great! It only counts full flights going up and doesn't get tricked by elevators.
The pedometer is very good, though like most wrist ones it's far from perfect. I'd say it's the best we've used.
The ability to see steps, stairs, etc... on the screen is great. You don't really need to always use a phone to know your progress
Bluetooth phone integration is surprisingly useful (she doesn't always have her ringer on or have her phone on her person, so she no longer misses calls!

Cons:
Heart rate tracking is cool in theory, but it tends to read high (always 90bpm or higher). My wife has remarkably fair skin (almost clear), which I though would help, but perhaps too much!
The thing is bulky. There's no getting around that this is more a watch than a bracelet.
Proprietary (or at least very uncommon) charger--boo!

I'm still giving this 5 stars overall, but consider the version without the heart rate tracking as just about as good as this.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in))

I am 6'3" and currently weigh 225 Lbs. Not a lightweight but as my Pulmonologist informs me "you're no longer clinically obese, you're just obese". Thanks Doc! A left-handed compliment if I ever heard one.

And there lies the rub. The first time I shook this out I had mild difficulty in getting the tabs and latches to hook up-- like I did just now. That seems to inspire a little less confidence in how safely it will support me without crashing down. Once it is expanded and set up it appears to be pretty sturdy. The color also makes it easy to see in the yard.

But having just had double knee replacement I was a bit concerned that it would hold me without making me faceplant in the yard. When I asked my wife to watch me sit on it in the kitchen she said "don't do that!". The sight of me pulling it out and clicking it together didn't inspire confidence in her either.

It did hold me while sitting still although I was a bit reluctant to shift my weight around on it. That would be my major sticking point. On a yard that is not completely level I know that I would have to be careful. The other part of that is that leaning forward or to one side suddenly puts additional stress on whichever part of the base is sitting on the ground. I am not convinced that leaning over wouldn't cause the stool to buckle and me to fall over.

So there it is. It seems to be a smart design and should solve the problem of having a stool available when needed. However plastic is not indestructible and will often bend as it is stressed over and over again. Good idea, decent execution, but it doesn't inspire any confidence for someone my size.

SUV Tent Car Camping Car Tent - Tailgate Tent SUV Tents for Camping, PU4000mm Waterproof, 1-4 Person Sleeping Capacity, Car Tents for Automobiles Car Awning My wife and I are not campers, but when we get out to the beach and parks we like to have something that provides shade and privacy. Where umbrellas and some sun shades are good, we'd been keeping our eyes open for something that might go on the car - expanding our options - and so when I had the chance to grab this SUV Tent Car Camping Car Tent I took it. So far we are pleased... but have a couple... concerns.

It's been a few weeks since we got this SUV Tent Car Camping Car Tent and after having several plans and attempts at even just testing it derailed by weather and wind, we finally had a chance to set it up in a parking lot - not at all ideal, but we at least got to see if it's what we were hoping for. With the weather changing we should be out on the beach sooner than later and we ARE feeling positive this SUV Tent Car Camping Car Tent will be a great addition to our gear.

1. It comes in a nice green bag to fit the tent and support items (poles, stakes).
Pro: It's a great bag to a point, matches the tent, and should make it easier to get this thing around.
Con: It JUST fits the gear so you have to get that tent back down tight. The tent set is heavier than we expected. Not so much we can't get it to the beach - but in that case we'll be with the car - in other words, you'll notice the weight. We do have a wagon we use for longer hauls.

2. It is mainly for the car or truck attachment, but we think we could use it on its own.
Pro: It would be nice to have it stand alone for those times we don't have the car access, and we THINK we could do that.
Con: There is a big hole where it would attach to the car. Would be nice if they had another layer similar to the front awning that you could use - or like the netting - and allow you to enclose the back as well. But alas, it's going to be open.
We are not sure how strong or sturdy it'll be without the car to support it - especially in any kind of wind.

3. Putting it up: not too bad.
Pro: Instructions are average, but there is some level of initiative here that helps get it up.
The poles are easy to put together
The poles are - mostly - easily inserted into the tent and - with two people.
The tent is made sturdily enough that it should last a decent amount of time - holding the poles in their track and forming the tent.
There seems to be enough pieces to give it good form and maintain that.
The straps to hold it to the car are pretty good and one can adapt - for example it says to attach to a roof rack, which we do not have, so we went with putting them into the door of the car and this held them securely and easily.
Con: We had both looked at the pics on the product page so knew what it should look like, but the instructions are average at best.

NOTE: We (again) were unable to get to the beach or park to try this, so it was set up on the edge of a parking lot with fairly bad grass. So we did NOT actually extend it 100% and lock it down nor did we step inside so as not to damage it. But from all we did do, it DOES appear like it will be a great option for us and that it will stay upright.

4. Laying it out & materials
Pro: In a parking lot it was fine, but of course we were being kind to it, trying not to damage it. The materials seem strong enough to take that kind of set up, but would be nicer all around on grass or sand.
The materials of the tent are nice - we like the bright green which will make it easy to spot.
The poles seem well made.
Con: While the tent, poles, and stakes seem like they are well made and with decent materials, we noticed that upon returning everything to the bag, the bag's stitching was already tearing. This was NOT there when we began and my wife felt popping as she pushed everything back inside, meaning it happened at this point.
So what do that mean for the tent? Is it the same materials? Will it last better? Will that stitching pop?
The bag is a pretty important part to this set as you're going to want to store and carry this SUV Tent Car Camping Car Tent within it. So... it does concern us. BUT we THINK the tent itself is a better quality of stitching. Time will tell.

5. Ready for use
Pro: We both felt like the inside had some great room and that once we can step in, we're going to find it gives us everything we need and are looking for. Again, on this pavement and grassy area we used we did NOT want to cause damage - it also made us discuss having a ground cloth under it to help protect the tent materials.
So looking inside, spending some time discussing it, we feel like we're going to have the privacy we want, the shade we need in the summer sun, and the size that allows us to have chairs, food, and whatever we want.
The tent also gives us an option for car camping. We are NOT campers, but sometimes talk about going with my sister-in-law and her family and with the right mattress in the back of our Prius, we think it might be fun. This tent would give us that privacy and space for day time, but also something around us for nights. We actually are talking about giving it a try.

We did not put up the awning for the front, but it was nice giving the inside added privacy - it is attached to itself on the sides via velcro, then to the top as a permanent attachment - you add the included stacks and can have it up as an awning or keep it as-is and use it for the front of the tent, over the included netting. Really well designed idea.

So in the end, we both really like this SUV Tent Car Camping Car Tent. It was very much or at least very similar to what we had been thinking and looking for. Something for the car, gives us privacy, shade, and potential for car camping. Easy to set up. Looks nice. Great space inside.

The reason for the 4 stars over the 5 is that 1. the bag tore on first returning of the tent to the bag. 2. The back side hole. It would be much better to have something like the netting at least to give that side some closure. 3. Better instructions would be helpful.

But in the end we both love this SUV Tent Car Camping Car Tent and if it lasts (much longer than the bag) we will be thrilled with the find - we are already, but... - and feel like we are going to get some great use out of it.

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in)) This fitbit counts steps well. The sleep tracking is far from perfect, but it does the job well enough to be useful. The stairs tracking function is a bit suspect, but ok for the most part. But if you want just those features, then there are other, much cheaper models that do the job. If you're thinking about getting the HR model, it's because you're interested in tracking heart rate, and this is where this fitbit fails miserably.

If you're just sitting around, it tracks your HR quite well, but of course you're not really that interested in your HR when you're just sitting around.
If you're long distance running at a steady pace, it's in the ballpark. If you're running intervals, the average of the entire workout is somewhat close to reality, but it averages your HR over a long timespan, so your peaks will be way too low (and too late), and your valleys will be too low (and too late). So for that, it's kinda useless.

Worst of all, if you're planning on tracking your heart rate while doing any non-running exercise like calisthenics, aerobics, weight training, or body-weight exercises, then forget about it. It's utterly useless in this department. Your HR readings will be either completely off, or it won't read your HR at all. It's kind of a known fact that when you do exercises where your forearm muscles move a lot, the Charge HR fails miserably, but even when doing planks, crunches, and other exercises where the arm is pretty much stationary, my HR readings are 30-50 points low, or just not displayed at all. These results are regardless of where I put the band. I've tried close and far from my wrist, on the inside or outside of the forearm, with different amounts of tightness, and even my leg. Readings are unusable regardless.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in))

text_fidelity_a:
Night Cat Life Jackets for Adults Kayaking Boating Vests Inflatable Lifesaving PFD, Survival Preservers, Lightweight Premium Quality, Automatic and Manual, 150KG (330LB) Night Cat [CE Approved] Life Jackets for Adults Kayaking Boating Vests Inflatable Lifesaving PFD, Survival Preservers, Lightweight Premium Quality, Automatic and Manual, 150KG/330LBS.
Sold by Nightcat-fishing $74.99

NOTE: We bought two of these life jackets in 2020, to use kayaking. Just bought another (March 2022) for a different family member. We have used them 2 years now, and are very satisfied with the product.

ORIGINAL 2020 REVIEW: I was looking for a more comfortable life jacket for flat water kayaking... our rigid foam Type II and Type III whitewater life vests were just too bulky, hot, and uncomfortable. These Night Cat inflatable vests were just the ticket: Slim, lightweight, and comfortable, all at a very reasonable price-point.

In particular, I liked: (1) the zipper pocket in the outer case that can hold a cell phone (it will accept a device up to 6.5 inches long); (2) the neoprene fabric collar that prevents the vest from chafing your neck; (3) the SOLAS-rated reflectors on the outside of the vest (there are reflectors on the air bladder also). BONUS: They come with a nice mesh and clear plastic storage bag.

This vest is perfect for recreational boating or other water activities conducted on relatively calm waters. The vests are very well made... almost identical to similar products costing 2 - 4 times as much. They arrive fully-charged and ready-to-use.

To be clear, the Night Cat vests do NOT carry a U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) approval label. These vests are CE approved, which means they meet standards recognized by most European countries (the vests also have an Australian certification).

Based upon the specifications of this vest (CE approved for off-shore use; will turn many (but not all) unconscious persons to a safe, face out-of-water position; 150 Newtons minimum buoyancy; hold full inflation for a minimum of 24 hours), these Night Cat vests are EQUIVALENT in performance to a USCG TYPE II inflatable personal flotation device (PFD) [i.e., a buoyant vest for general boating on calm near-shore and inland waters where fast rescue is likely].

However, if you absolutely must, by applicable federal, state, or local rules, have a USCG-approved PFD for your type of craft or activity, you may have to get something else... without a USCG approval label, the Night Cat vests probably would not satisfy these regulatory requirements.

For flat and calm water activities where a USCG-approved life vest is not mandated, these Night Cat life vests are perfect.

[NOTE 2]: From someone with technical rescue experience... if you are going to be far off-shore, in whitewater, or in swift water where there's the potential for "strainers", wear (as appropriate) a Type I, Type II, or Type III (or if applicable, a Type V) rigid foam life jacket
text_fidelity_b: Night Cat Life Jackets for Adults Kayaking Boating Vests Inflatable Lifesaving PFD, Survival Preservers, Lightweight Premium Quality, Automatic and Manual, 150KG (330LB)

text_fidelity_a:
POC, Ventral Air MIPS Road Cycling Helmet with Performance Cooling We recently got an electric scooter, plus my wife rides roller blades, and we’re talking about an electric bike - or recumbent, not sure which. We have a need for a couple bike helmets. I will fully admit, we are NOT experts in this area and have done no research beyond knowing they need to be rated and that there are good ones and bad. We have each owned in the past - that kind that looks similar to this, but with that point at the back, which always makes us think, what happens if you land on the back and that point slams the helmet forward...

So when I had the chance to grab this POC Ventral Air MIPS (CPSC) I took it without hesitation. Not only does it look good, but in wearing it, it feels great and gives us a sense of being safer than without a helmet. And for all the helmets we have owned, that this has the blunted back, answers that “what if,”

So this POC Ventral Air MIPS (CPSC) arrived and we broke in right away - had to see it in person. We were blown away by the presentation - it comes in a nice box - make sure to take care of this box, it is your storage box! Inside you’ll find the helmet and a bag. Open up and the helmet goes in the bag in the box - it is a GREAT way to store your helmet! Our previous helmets always end up on a shelf somewhere. This is excellent and we were already impressed.

Next... the helmet. It looks cool. Not only the color - I’m a blue guy and it’s perfect - but the overall design is so cool. We both liked the matted look - over the glossy really - but in person it looks even better. And on, it looks seriously cool. I tried it with both my reading glasses - no point other than to see how well it handles glasses - and my sunglasses - one of several I own, so one design style - and in both cases they fit perfectly under the sides of the helmet. I felt like I could wear them for an hour and have no rub or discomfort. I have not actually worn them out riding yet, but in this situation, the test was impressive.

As to that idea we always wondered about - what happens if you land on the back and that point - this is blunted, meaning there is no point. You land and it makes sense - you’ll have the back side make contact, but in a way that appears it’ll cushion the head and not shove it or the helmet forward.

The helmet is really light weight and you cannot believe how it feels like it could be that light and protect your head. So we put it on... and for me it fit perfectly. I got the large due to my large head. I had to open the strap slightly, but one half turn on the wheel and it was perfect - snug, but not tight nor uncomfortable. Now we only have this one, so when my wife went out to test the scooter, she had to wear this one. She has a much smaller head than mine, but it was nothing to size this down for her - while she technically doesn’t fit their size chart at this size, it worked well - she was comfortable and felt completely secure in it. It was very easy to size down for her, then bring it back up for me. It was easy and quick and we both felt great with it on.

I’ll be honest - this price point is above what we would normally spend. I was able to get it as a Vine Reviewer and for that I am grateful. I normally do not speak to price because of that, but in this case, wish to address it. In talking about it, we WOULD spend the money to get a second one for her. We feel that the safety this “promises” is worth the money. Now that said, We would do much more research first - we are not experts on the safety aspects of helmets and would make sure first. There is NO way we would go out and test this - meaning risk our head to see that is does what it promises. But if our further research shows what we think it would, yes, we would consider spending the money. Brain safety is important and we want something good. Now that said, if there is a product at a lower price that provides equal safety, we would seriously consider that - money is something we are careful with, but so too our safety. In the end, this is an excellent helmet that fits well and comfortably. Safety is the priority. But we do have to be realistic about cost. So if we could afford it and our research indicates it is a value, then yes, we would pay, but if not, if we found something as good at a lower price point, we’d have to look in that direction.

But we both love this POC Ventral Air MIPS (CPSC) helmet and are thrilled to have it.
text_fidelity_b: POC, Ventral Air MIPS Road Cycling Helmet with Performance Cooling

KastKing Sharky Baitfeeder III Spinning Reel 10+1 Shielded Stainless Steel BB - Carbon Fiber Drag for Live Liner Bait Fishing Action I don't write many reviews - typically when I do they are positive. I'm pretty disappointed. My wife bought me this this reel to go fishing with my kids for Father's Day. I had been reading about these Kastking bait feeders and it was much less expensive than a known Shimano. I watched some youtube videos about it that seemed pretty good and the amazon reviews seemed real good. We got to the pier and I had them spool it up with 20# mono. I like having my spools wound by the machine - it does a better job. The drag cap came off but it was difficult to remove. It seems like it took a good 2 minutes to unscrew... NOW it will not go back on - it freely spins and won't attach.
I posted a photo I can't tell if it's stripped or what is going on inside there. The threading appears to be fine.
The old timers that work at the pier fooled with it but said that's what I get for buying unknown name brands. I told them everyone started out unknown! I recently bought a penn battle II rod / reel combo and the rod was defective from the factory.
I wasted my $6 to get her spooled up with line but the worst part I didn't get to try out my new reel on father's day - I was really excited to use it! I'm glad I didn't get the other spool loaded up with braided line like I was thinking - I'd have been out another $30...
If the Kastking people make good on the replacement I'll test it out and will consider changing my rating. Right now I'm disappointed and wanted to gripe. Anticlimactic!
Is this rare or typical? We'll find out! Looking at other ratings seems like it might be rare (I hope). I'll update as things progress. - Wayne

Sportsvoutdoors Trekking Pole, Telescopic Collapsible Anti-Shock Climbing Stick With EVA Handle for Hiking/Walking/Trekking (Black) I could have gotten something similar to this telescopic cane locally, and for nearly the same price. But this one appeared to have some advantages the others didn't. There wasn't any instructions on using this cane, but it wasn't too hard to figure out. To adjust the length there are three sections which can be pulled out to make the cane longer. The cane in it's fully collapsed state is 21" long, fully extended its 42". To change the lengths you twist the shafts which loosen or tighten the assembly depending on the direction you twist. You can actually pull out a section completely if you're not careful (it slips back in pretty easily). The tip of the cane is interesting. There is a rubber foot that can be removed which exposes a small diameter metal point, that I assume is for use on icy surfaces (we don't get that too often here in Texas). There is another thing that can be screwed on the end of the cane, some sort of round dome looking thing, I haven't a clue what it's purpose might be.

Over-all I happy with the walking stick, I like that it collapses down like it does for easy storage & carrying. And that it feels like pretty solid support when in use. I'm happy with my purchase.

The kubbs, stakes, and batons are all very well made and I would imagine will hold up well for some time. We've only played a few practice games with my small family but this summer I expect this will be a hit at our huge family reunion. I can't wait to get everyone together to play! Fitness Reality Squat Rack Power Cage with | Optional LAT Pulldown & Leg Holdown Attachment | Squat and Bench Rack Combos| Super Max 810 XLT | I'm extremely pleased with the product. Assembly was straightforward and all the holes lined up! Very sturdy construction.

The attached pictures show an addition I made to turn give the rack a cable-crossover functionality. These pictures represent my Version 1.0.

All the parts can be purchased at Lowes. The rack has two perfect attachment points for the pulleys. See picture 1. This shows a threaded eye bolt and 1 1/2" fixed pulley. Two lock nuts hold it in place but it is purposely NOT tight so it has the ability to rotate. Picture 2 shows a length of zinc coated square steel tubing from Lowes. Three threaded eye bolts connect the additional cables to the center cable on the rack. Picture 3 shows me pulling on the two handles.

I think this works really well. Keep in mind, this is Version 1. One could probably cut the steel tubing length down. With the full length, it doesn't seem to hit the cage but it potentially could. NOTE: I did try this without the steel tubing and I didn't like the feel. As one completes the motion, the angle change in the cables was significant enough to notice. Your mileage may vary and you may prefer that characteristic. That tubing was the most expensive piece at about $20. Everything else is dirt cheap.

If you decide to try something like this, please be EXTREMELY careful. I am a Mechanical Engineer by education so this was something I was comfortable doing. Review the load limits of ALL the components you intend to use. For instance, the two fixed pulleys from Lowes have a safe working load of 420 pounds. I used 1/8" vinyl coated braided wire rope. Blue Hawk brand with a safe working load of 340 pounds.

Make sure ANY carabiners you use to make connections are rated for HIGH LOAD and NOT for hanging keys on your belt loop. I can't stress this enough. You do NOT want something breaking on you during full extension.

IMPORTANT: Make sure you terminate the ends of the cables correctly. Properly swaged deformable collars are likely the best approach but I used a threaded clamp for this setup. I will likely change to a swaged connection because the clamping hardware can rub against your arm during use. Also, use thimbles on the ends of both cables to protect the cable attachment points.
text_fidelity_b: Fitness Reality Squat Rack Power Cage with | Optional LAT Pulldown & Leg Holdown Attachment | Squat and Bench Rack Combos| Super Max 810 XLT |

I guess everyone else is not using the incline feature.  And no...I am not 8 feet tall....with long legs. Only 5'10" and my wife is 5'1" and has the same issue. Feyachi HL-20 Pistol Light Compact 400 Lumens Weapon Light Pistol Flashlight Tactical Handgun Rail Mount Flashlight Testing this light everything worked as the company says. The box included 4 CR123a batteries. You only need 2 for powering the light. Putting the batteries in place takes some talent by aligning the cover back to the base while the batteries are pressing against it. It is just a bit tricky but the cover will snap in place while holding with one hand and you can snap the lock with the other hand. The on/off switch in my opinion is in a good location. I also like that it stays out of the way from your finger until you need it.

Also the flashlight comes with additional clips for mounting it on a Picatinnny rail. The use of the clips will depend on what kind of hunting item you will be using it on. The stock one that came installed worked for me. They are easy to change out by removing a screw on the flashlight side. The included clips may also allow for how close you want the on /off switch to your finger.

Final thoughts: I like this brand and model. I also feel it is in a fair price range. The light is bright and should last a long time before having to replace the batteries. One more note is that to replace batteries, the flashlight will need to be taken off the Picatinny rail. I am giving this Feyachi flashlight 5 stars for good quality construction, value and brightness.

text_fidelity_a:
Covacure Beach Towels Lightweight Travel Towel Set, Quick Dry Towel (63"x32") & Carrying Bag for Beach, Travel, Swim, Pool, Camping, Outdoors and Sports Towel This a handy towel for mobile adventures. It isn't as fluffy and snuggly as a thick cotton bath towel, but it's really absorbent, dries quicker, and rolls up into a much smaller bundle, making it a great alternative for taking along when space is limited.

The towel's compact portability is one of it's strongest features. It comes neatly folded and rolled up in a nylon and mesh drawstring bag. It's a bit of a thrash getting it back into the stuff sack folded up if you don't roll it nice and tight. I find it far easier to just stuff it in like you would a sleeping bag, starting with one corner of the towel and packing it in tight starting at the bottom. The packed bag measures about 8 inches long and 5 inches in diameter, so it takes up lots less room in your duffel bag or backpack than a regular towel. I've attached a photo of the packed towel in my hand to give you an idea of its size.

The towel is just over 5 feet long and not quite 3 feet wide. If you use it to lay on at the beach, your feet will end up in the sand, and not on the towel, unless you're under 5 feet tall.

The microfiber fabric is quite absorbent, easily drying me completely after a shower.

It also dries faster than my normal cotton bath towel. There's an elastic loop crudely sewn onto one corner of the towel to hang it by (see attached photo). I don't usually use the loop because you need a pretty high hook to keep the towel off the ground when you hang it by the loop. Instead, I just hang it by the middle across a peg or hook to dry.

The biggest drawback I've noticed is the feel of the towel aganst my skin. Instead of the soft, snuggly fluff of a regular bath or beach towel, this towel feels more like a sheet of suede or chamois leather. For that reason, it won't replace my bath towel at home, but I do think that it's a reasonable compromise for an efficient travel accessory. It seems particularly useful for carrying to the beach or pool, and for camping or adventure travel (staying in hostels, for example) where you'll need to provide your own towel.
If that's the kind of stuff you do, this towel should work well for you.

Let me know if you found anything in my review helpful.
text_fidelity_b: Covacure Beach Towels Lightweight Travel Towel Set, Quick Dry Towel (63"x32") & Carrying Bag for Beach, Travel, Swim, Pool, Camping, Outdoors and Sports Towel

text_fidelity_a:
Bushwhacker Omaha - Bicycle Grocery Pannier Cycling Rack Basket Bike Rear Bag Rear Accessories - Sold as Pair Some background - I purchased an electric Pedego Interceptor bicycle for my better half. Pedego's frame also serves as a bike rack, and does an awesome job of protecting the battery. The challenge is that tubing is so thick, that 99% of all panniers will not work because the pannier hooks won't fit over the frame tubing. So, I bought a Topeak Uni Super Tourist Fat Disc Frame Mounted Bicycle Rack to mount above the existing Pedego rack. There was some custom work involved, but it turned out great! This pannier fits perfectly on to the Topeak rear rack.

I needed a folding pannier that a standard backpack would fit into, to make it easier just to plop a backpack into the bike (instead of having to load the panniers everytime, then take all the stuff out afterwards). I did a lot of research, and there are very few folding-grocery panniers that have the width of the Bushwacker (Dimensions: 14" Length x 9" width x 10.25" height). Of those that are also this jumbo size, I read that most do not hold their shape very well when loaded up.

This Bushwacker is rock solid, having steel-reinforced tubing to hold it in place. It has a nice bungee-hook set-up to keep it secure, and is adjustable to increase tension.

Tips:
1) If you use a backpack in this pannier, use a good carabiner (we used the sturdy, easy-to-open-and close, Black Diamond Oval Caribiner) to help prevent the backpack from flying out when hitting bumps. Simply plop the backpack into the pannier, attach the carabiner to the top loop of the backpack, and then hook it on the cloth handle of the pannier. Another option would be to use a bungee cord through the backpack, and attach the bungee to the frame.

2) To help prevent theft of this nice pannier when the bicycle is parked, I attached a small cable to the handle (OnGuard Akita Seat Leash Cable - 53 cm x 5 mm), and locked the seat leash to another cable (used to lock the bike seat to the frame). Though it's a very thin seat leash cable, which could probably be snipped easily, it does help prevent someone without tools just walking off with it. Next, I used some heavy duty zip ties to attach the plastic clips (bottom / backside of pannier) to the Topeak rack. So, I don't take the pannier on & off the bike - I just leave it in place.

FYI - I only used one of these panniers (keeping the other as a backup). On the other side of the bike, I built a custom, locking, waterproof hardshell pannier out of a Pelican 1430 case. It's awesome, and it's great to store the heavy chain & u-lock, tools, extra tube, pump, lights, and extra batteries. I used the terrific latching mechanism from Arkel (10 inch length), and also used a seat leash and zip ties to secure it in place (I leave this pannier on the bike also). Happy riding!
text_fidelity_b: Bushwhacker Omaha - Bicycle Grocery Pannier Cycling Rack Basket Bike Rear Bag Rear Accessories - Sold as Pair

text_fidelity_a: Schwinn Fitness 430 Elliptical Trainer [Discontinued] Before making this purchase, I did my homework in reading reviews and trying out several other ellipticals at fitness stores.  Some of them had an awkward stride motion, others were noise, some were too big, and others were too expensive.  The Schwinn 430 has been just perfect for us.  It relatively compact and has a nice smooth motion to the stride.  It did start to squeak a day or two after we bought and assembled it.  However, after I sprayed the track with white lithium lubricant (lift the wheels off the track and let it dry before bringing the wheels back to the track)the squeak has gone away.  It doesn't have a lot of the extra bells and whistles such as an ipod connection or a fan, but those items could be introduced externally.  Also the monitor is a little difficult to read.  None of those factors really matter to me.  It just seems to be a well built, basic, compact elliptical.  Some reviewers also commented that it was difficult to assemble.  I did not find that to be the case.  We put it together in a couple hours one evening.
text_fidelity_b: Schwinn Fitness 430 Elliptical Trainer [Discontinued]

text_fidelity_a:
Elimoons Silicone Wedding Ring for Men - 10 Rings&Singles Silicone Rubber Wedding Bands- 8.7 mm Wide - 2.5mm Thick I’ve had my eye on another brand for awhile, but wasn’t sure - a single ring is around $25 - being concerned the silicone wouldn’t work, feel good, or have any give. My ring finger tapers and can go up and down during the day, so metal rings can go from loose to tight. Would this kind work? While not metal pricing, I still didn’t want to pay for another ring to sit in the drawer.

I am thrilled with these rings.

First, I got two sets: I literally fell on the line between the two sizes so figured it would be smarter than risking it. My ring finger is the smaller of the two, but I still get use of the larger set on other fingers. Usually not at the same time - looks a little goofy.

Second, I wasn’t sure on the grip - would they work on my tapered finger and would they have any give. Yes to both. In fact the only time I have an “issue” with being loose is washing my hands. I have to watch a bit, holding fingers tight, but otherwise the rings both stay snug and on, as well as give a little when humidity expands them. I love the fit, the size and look on my finger, and that little give.

Third, Yes, I keep them on when washing my hands, but I do take the ring off to dry it as well. Otherwise it will retain moisture - it does get annoying and loosens the fit. I have worn them to shower, but now keep it off, just in case.

Forth, working out and doing things with them on is a breeze. I lift weights (with/without gloves) play pickle ball, do chores, you name it, and the rings hold up. There is no issue and I don’t have to worry about damaging, bending, or otherwise having any problems.

Fifth, The Colors... Interesting. Some I love and look really nice on their own and on my hand. Some I just don’t like. It’s a personal taste thing, but some look cartoonish or goofy. Overall, it’s a personal thing, so have some fun. I was surprised I liked the look of the bright blue, red (thought I’d hate it), and tie dye.

Sixth, there is a slight difference between the cuts of these two sets I got. I include image to show: one is rounded, the other sharp cut. Not sure you can tell from product page the difference - I didn’t until they arrived.

These are some great rings for the price and I do like that I got different sizes. I do wear the larger ones on other fingers from time to time, but I love that I can now wear a wedding ring and not worry. (* Same review given for the other set in order to stay consistent with my experience)
text_fidelity_b: Elimoons Silicone Wedding Ring for Men - 10 Rings&Singles Silicone Rubber Wedding Bands- 8.7 mm Wide - 2.5mm Thick
